memos.risk:
Risk officer assessment: I recommend refusing any size.

The brief has no clean entry. The coin is down 87% from its 30-minute high and 65% over 30 minutes, with net outflow over the last 15 minutes and a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.96 in the post-graduation window. A launch bot was present, and the first two minutes saw 178 SOL of buying. The curve is moderately concentrated (bundle share 17%, completer share 17%), and the pool is thin at about 61 SOL, so a $20 round trip would eat much of the 1.4-5.1% cost band and more on exit.

Nothing here supports a buy. If the desk wants a tripwire: revisit only if the coin shows a sustained recovery with positive net flow over several intervals and depth that can absorb a $5 ticket with a 30% stop and a 15-minute hold. Until then, skip.
memos.scout:
I can't make a strong case for buying this coin. The brief shows a 87% drawdown from its 30-minute high, a -65% return over 30 minutes, and in the last 15 minutes sell SOL ($132.6) slightly exceeded buy SOL ($126.4), with net outflow of -6.2 SOL and more sellers (326) than buyers (306). The first two minutes after graduation also show a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.96, meaning distribution is happening roughly as fast as demand arrives.

The few points that could be read as positive are the "ORGANIC" classification with no airdrop dump seen, a moderate top-3 holder share (8%), and a 60 SOL pool. Buyer count is high at 705, and the curve shows no obvious single-operator concentration. But none of that establishes that demand will persist 30-60 minutes out. Recent demand is fading, not building, and the price is already far below its high.

Verdict: no honest case for buying now. Skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a slow bleed plus fees, not a clean rug. The coin is down 65% over 30 minutes and 87% from its 30-minute high, with a -25% return over the last 15 minutes. Sellers (326) outnumbered buyers (306), and sell SOL ran at about 0.96 of buy SOL in the first two minutes after graduation (132.58 sold vs 126.36 bought in the last 15 min, net flow -6.22 SOL). That is distribution into a thin pool of 60.74 SOL depth, where a $20 round trip costs 1.4-5.1% before any move. A bounce of 5% would barely cover fees, and dead-cat bounces rarely hold after an 87% drawdown. The bundle share (17%) and a launch bot present point to early sniping that is now exiting. Skip.
